bandSystemAssessment.convention: 01_doc_conventions.md specifies `<NN>_<snake_case_title>.md` where NN is a two-digit prefix from the band table in 00_README.md, using the lowest available number in the appropriate band. Sub-letters (30a_, 42a_) are for tightly-coupled children. Subdirectories are 'reserved for things that are inherently a series', and the key rule is stated explicitly: 'The band number reserves the slot — 80_adrs/ IS the 80-band content, 90_runbooks/ IS the 90-band content.' Inside a subdirectory, files need no numeric prefix and use a domain-appropriate pattern. The band table (00_README.md, last_updated 2026-05-27): 00-09 Meta; 10-19 Ground truth/architecture/roadmap; 20-29 Agent operating rules/dev flow/workstation/deploy; 30-39 SmartCity OS; 40-49 Design Accelerator + Revit Connector; 50-59 Hauska SDK; 60-69 ECI; 70-79 Bizops + brokerage; 80-89 ADRs; 90-99 Runbooks, postmortems, incident records.

collisions.type: semantic collision, not a filename collision
collisions.finding: Two directories claim slot 80. The doc-conventions rule 'the band number reserves the slot' means 80_adrs/ IS the 80 slot, so 80_meetings/ is a second claimant. It is also a SEMANTIC violation independent of the numbering: the band table assigns 80-89 to 'ADRs (architecture decision records)' with no allowance for meeting transcripts. Otter transcripts are primary-source records, not architecture decisions. No band in the table fits raw counterparty transcripts, so this is a MISSING BAND expressed as a collision. Note both directories can coexist on the filesystem — nothing is broken today; the cost is that a future agent applying the band table literally cannot place a new transcript.

collisions.type: semantic collision, not a filename collision
collisions.finding: Two directories claim slot 90. The band table reads '90-99 Runbooks, postmortems, incident records' and the conventions doc names 90_runbooks/ and 91_postmortems/ explicitly as examples — so 90_runbooks/ holds slot 90 and 91_postmortems/ holds slot 91 with sanction. 90_operations/ has NO sanction in either doc: it is the largest single directory in this assigned set (47 files), it holds both plans of record, and it did not exist when the README band table was last updated (2026-05-27). It should almost certainly own 92_ (the lowest free slot in the 90-99 band) or the band table should be amended to name it. This is the clearest case in the repo of the doc set outgrowing its own index.

nonCollisions.finding: NO COLLISION — verified, not assumed. I checked for competing root files at each of these prefixes (`ls -1 19*.md 24*.md 64*.md 65*.md 80*.md 90*.md 91*.md` at root) and the result was EMPTY: not one root .md uses prefix 19, 24, 64, 65, 80, 90, or 91. I then enumerated every root .md prefix (`ls -1 *.md | cut -c1-2 | sort | uniq -c`) and confirmed the same by construction — root files run 00-18, 20-23, 25-33, 40-63, 70-79, and skip exactly the seven prefixes the directories occupy. So each of these four directories cleanly and exclusively reserves its slot, which is precisely the behavior the conventions doc prescribes. An empty result here is a real finding, not an absence of evidence: I searched the full root .md set.

semanticDrift: 19_hardware_sovereignty/ sits in the 10-19 'Ground truth, portfolio architecture, roadmap' band. Hardware sovereignty is a positioning-and-pitch asset, not ground truth or roadmap. It is the last slot in the band, which reads like it was placed by availability rather than fit.

24_adaptive_ui/ sits in the 20-29 'Agent operating rules, AI-first dev flow, workstation, deploy rules' band. Adaptive UI is a product-surface design discipline with no relationship to agent operating rules. Clear misfit.

64_recursive_loop/ and 65_sensors/ both sit in the 60-69 band, which the table assigns entirely to 'ECI' (Empressa Company Intelligence, the internal dogfood app). Neither is ECI. The recursive-improvement program is portfolio-wide meta-process; the sensor program is a cross-vertical product program. Two of the three occupied slots in the ECI band are not ECI.

Root-level unnumbered strays exist outside the scheme entirely: CLAUDE.md, _STATE.md, HAUSKA_COMMERCIALIZATION_VISION.md, HAUSKA_INVESTOR_BRIEF.md, network_effects_use_cases_and_gaps.md, temporal_context_engine_spec.md. CLAUDE.md and _STATE.md are legitimate harness/state files. The other four are canonical-shaped content with no band slot.

_land_records/README.md documents the failure mode in its own words: 'this set was originally drafted at root numeric slots 10/52/53/54/90 and adr_020, all of which collided with existing canonical docs. Reconciled into _land_records/.' This is primary evidence that the band system is at capacity pressure and that authors resolve collisions by escaping into underscore folders.
bandSystemAssessment.verdict: PARTIAL. Mechanically the system holds: zero filename collisions exist anywhere, every numbered directory exclusively owns its prefix, and the subdirectory-reserves-the-slot rule is respected. Semantically it has drifted materially. The band table (last_updated 2026-05-27) predates 90_operations/, 64_recursive_loop/, 65_sensors/, and portfolio_thesis/, and does not describe them; four of the nine numbered directories sit in bands whose stated subject they do not match; and the documented workaround for a full band is to leave the numbering system entirely for an underscore folder — which is now the majority pattern (14 underscore dirs vs 9 numbered dirs in this assigned set alone). The system is not broken, it is UNMAINTAINED: the index has not been updated as the repo grew. The cheap, high-value fix is amending the 00_README.md band table to describe reality and assigning 90_operations/ a free slot; the expensive fix nobody needs is renumbering.
bandSystemAssessment.basis: Read 01_doc_conventions.md (lines 1-200, covering File naming, Sub-letters, Subdirectories, Frontmatter, Status semantics) and 00_README.md (full, including the verbatim Numbering bands code fence). Verified collisions empirically with `ls -1d [0-9]*/`, `ls -1 19*.md 24*.md 64*.md 65*.md 80*.md 90*.md 91*.md` (empty), and a full root-prefix histogram. Corroborated the capacity-pressure claim with the self-documented slot-collision note in _land_records/README.md.

smartsiteMastersVerdict.whatItIs: A complete, finished, self-declared authoritative reference set for Smart Site (the customer-facing product formerly called Property Explorer): 9 numbered masters covering positioning, three white papers at three audience altitudes (market/substance/technical), a product walkthrough, GTM audiences and pricing, a bizdev FAQ, and a glossary. Assembled 2026-08-04 from the ratified 2026-07-31 naming session, the product/GTM doc set, and a feature inventory of the live application.
smartsiteMastersVerdict.peerEvidence: This is not inferred from folder-name symmetry — BOTH READMEs state the relationship explicitly and reciprocally. _smartsite_masters/00_README.md: 'The companion set `_smartcity_masters/` governs the SmartCity OS product line sold to cities. The two share the smart-site unit and never share collateral: professional pitches come from this folder, city pitches from that one.' _smartcity_masters/00_README.md names the Smart Site white papers as one of its own source inputs and shares the ruling that 'a smart site is any addressable place, fully twinned; a smart city is a bunch of smart sites. It is the unit, not a product.' Structurally they are twins: same frontmatter shape (id/title/status/last_updated/applies_to/owner:nick/purpose), same authority claim ('these win; correct the other doc, not these'), same deliberate isolation from the numbered canon, same INTERNAL-ONLY marking discipline, same approved-claims-register and never-say-list mechanism, same two-altitude vocabulary rule.
smartsiteMastersVerdict.notSomethingElse: Ruled out the alternatives explicitly. It is NOT a scratch or draft staging area: all 9 files carry status: active with legal 4-value frontmatter and clean last_updated dates (8 at 2026-08-04, 06_gtm at 2026-08-10 — meaning it was EDITED four days ago and still not committed). It is NOT superseded by _smartcity_masters: the two govern different products for different buyers and their READMEs cross-reference as peers. It is NOT deliberately excluded for sensitivity: .gitignore contains no rule matching this path (verified with git check-ignore -v, which attributes ONLY the 2 PDFs to the repo-wide `*.pdf` rule at line 34 and returns nothing for the 9 .md files). It is NOT a symlink or submodule. The only remaining explanation is that it was never `git add`ed.
smartsiteMastersVerdict.basis: Read both 00_README.md files in full. Verified tracking with `git ls-files _smartsite_masters` (returns 0 rows) and `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard _smartsite_masters` (returns 11). Verified the ignore attribution with `git check-ignore -v` on both a .pdf and the .md set. Harvested frontmatter from all 9 .md.
smartsiteMastersVerdict.risk: HIGH and asymmetric. This folder is the single largest concentration of uncommitted authority in the repo. It is the governing definition of what may and may not be said about the customer-facing product — including the binding never-say list (never lead with digital twin, RWA, tokenization, blockchain, atom, substrate), the no-cycle-time/no-savings/no-ROI-figures rule, the no-3D-claims rule, and the 'nationwide United States' coverage ruling. If this clone is lost, a future agent producing Smart Site collateral has NO approved-claims register and no never-say list, and the failure is SILENT — nothing errors, the guardrails are simply absent and the agent improvises. The doc-staleness gate cannot catch it either, since the gate walks the filesystem rather than the index and these files are present locally. Compounding factor: OPS-17 binds 'a claim not in the approved-claims register of a master is not approved' on every lane artifact, so this program depends on a register that does not survive a clone.
smartsiteMastersVerdict.recommendation: Commit all 9 .md and the 2 brand SVGs. Then rule separately on the 2 PDFs, which are blocked by a `*.pdf` glob written for confidential title exemplars and are hitting product collateral as collateral damage — the same rule also ignores 5 SmartCity PDFs. The clean fix is narrowing the ignore rule to the confidential paths it was written for (e.g. `_title_exemplars_confidential/` plus specific patterns) rather than a repo-wide extension ban, so that legitimate collateral PDFs in both masters folders can be tracked.

findings.title: The status vocabulary is a schema gap, not 367 authoring errors
findings.detail: scripts/doc-staleness.mjs enforces 4 legal statuses (active|draft|superseded|historical) from 01_doc_conventions.md:93. It reports 367 vocab violations repo-wide, 63 in my directories alone. The pattern is uniform: operators write status as a rich sentence carrying real state ('operations doc (gap-closure: R-FND-2 registry-as-engine-input)', 'resume dispatch (SF-1 24 stale cleared; 5 promoted-but-cert-fail remain)') because the 4-value scheme cannot express dispatch or ADR lifecycle. 16 ADRs use accepted/proposed, which is correct ADR practice and illegal here. Flattening 32 informative 90_operations strings to 'active' would DESTROY state to satisfy a gate.
findings.evidence: node scripts/doc-staleness.mjs --json (read-only): vocabViolations 367 of 852 scanned. 63 fall in my directories: 32 in 90_operations/, 16 in 80_adrs/, 6 in _smartcity_masters/whitespace_package/, plus scattered others.
findings.recommendation: Extend the vocabulary (add accepted/proposed/superseded-in-part) or add a separate `kind:` field, and exempt 80_adrs/ and dispatch-shaped files. Fix the schema before the gate.

findings.evidence: 00_overview.md 'Superseded-home note (2026-06-21)'; frontmatter harvest of all 13; last commit 2026-07-05.
findings.recommendation: Operator ruling: unfreeze, supersede, or archive. Whichever way, encode it in status so an instrument can see it.

findings.title: Root .vercel/ links doc_repo itself as a Vercel project
findings.detail: Verbatim: {"projectId":"prj_2yoNzBuTjy4BT2rf92AcRJHo92Nx","orgId":"team_4TH5lNnFHcBGx4EKNapJ2MVG","projectName":"doc_repo"}. Distinct from system-overview-site/.vercel/ (projectName 'empressa-overview', same org). Most likely a `vercel link` run from the repo root instead of from the site subfolder. If a deploy ever ran from root it could publish the entire internal strategy repo — _decisions/, _prospects/, internal-only masters — to a public URL. Ignored via .gitignore:29, so invisible to a clone and harmless in-repo.
findings.evidence: cat .vercel/project.json vs system-overview-site/.vercel/project.json; git check-ignore -v attributes to .gitignore:29.
findings.recommendation: Check the Vercel dashboard for a stray 'doc_repo' project and delete it if unused. Not touched here, per the read-only constraint. Reinforces the standing 'vercel link --project first' memory.

findings.title: premortem-check skill is installed while its governing memory records it RETIRED
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md says 'Eight skills installed' and there are exactly 8 — the count matches. But the standing memory records premortem-check as RETIRED 2026-07-13 in favor of adversarial review, while .claude/skills/premortem-check/SKILL.md remains present and discoverable. CLAUDE.md also still instructs 'Use the premortem-check skill before any commitment' and 'never let a yellow from premortem-check slide'.
findings.evidence: find .claude -type f (8 SKILL.md); CLAUDE.md 'Four structural commitments' and 'Skills' sections vs the retirement memory.
findings.recommendation: Operator ruling: delete the skill and amend CLAUDE.md, or retire the memory. A retired practice that is still installed and still instructed will be used.

findings.title: 91_postmortems/ mis-statused against the repo's own convention, and the practice has lapsed
findings.detail: All 6 postmortems carry status: active and all 6 are flagged stale (87-101 days). 01_doc_conventions.md explicitly lists 'Postmortems' as an example of status: historical, so these are wrong by the repo's own rule and a 6-file edit clears 6 of the 131 repo-wide stale-active hits. Separately, no postmortem has been written since 2026-05-19 despite documented incidents since (the 2026-08-03 cortex-api key-rotation outage, the Bastrop B3-repealed-to-BDC edition incident cited in OPS-17). The practice appears to have migrated to _decisions/ and FINDING_ files in 90_operations/ without a ruling.
findings.evidence: Frontmatter harvest of all 6; doc-staleness --json staleActive; 01_doc_conventions.md status-semantics table.
findings.recommendation: Flip the 6 to historical. Separately rule on whether postmortems remain a practice or are formally absorbed into _decisions/.

findings.title: _smartcity_masters/onepagers_v2/ is the one frontmatter-free subtree in an otherwise strict reference set
findings.detail: 7 files with no frontmatter at all, inside the folder that most loudly claims authority and whose sibling onepager_briefs/ (8 files) is fully conformant. The v2 naming plus the missing frontmatter suggests an in-progress regeneration that was never finished or ratified. A collateral producer reading the folder cannot tell which of onepager_briefs/ or onepagers_v2/ is authoritative.
findings.evidence: Frontmatter harvest across _smartcity_masters: all 7 onepagers_v2/*.md return status=NONE, last_updated=NONE, while all 8 onepager_briefs/*.md carry active/2026-08-07.
findings.recommendation: Ratify v2 with frontmatter and supersede onepager_briefs/, or mark v2 draft. Currently ambiguous to any agent producing collateral.

findings.title: 90_operations/ fuses a standing operations manual with ~20 spent dispatch records
findings.detail: The OPS-0..OPS-17 numbered set plus OPS-INDEX_operator_manual.md is a durable manual. Interleaved in the same flat 47-file directory are ~20 point-in-time PHASE_C_*/PHASE_D_*/REBRAND_* dispatch and resume records whose useful life ended when they closed. This is the direct cause of the folder's 32 illegal status strings — dispatch lifecycle has no vocabulary. The existence of OPS-INDEX_operator_manual.md already implies the intended split.
findings.evidence: Full 47-file listing with status harvest; flat directory confirmed (find -mindepth 1 -type d returns empty).
findings.recommendation: Future cleanup: move closed dispatch records to a subfolder (e.g. 90_operations/dispatches_closed/) leaving the OPS-n manual clean. Out of scope for a cartography pass — flagged, not done.
